author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty filter in the request address and list only the veterinarians holding that specialty. The machine-readable form becomes a supported surface.
acceptance_criteria: With no specialty filter, the page at /vets.html and the machine-readable list at /vets behave exactly as they do today.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only those veterinarians, a page at a time.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, /vets?specialty=<name> returns only those veterinarians.
A filter differing from a specialty's name only by letter case matches that specialty.
A filter that is only part of a specialty's name matches no specialty; matching is on the whole name.
A filter no veterinarian's specialty matches succeeds with an empty veterinarian list, not an error.
An empty or whitespace-only filter behaves as if no filter were given, like the empty owner search.
Spaces around an otherwise valid specialty name are not removed before matching, so such a filter matches nothing.
On a filtered page spanning more than one page, the paging links carry the same filter.
non_goals: Any visible control for the filter on either form — no form, dropdown, or other page control; the filter is an address contract only
Free-text veterinarian search, and search over pets or visits — NG-9 stays declined in its narrowed form
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2)
Defining what a repeated specialty parameter does
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1. NG-9 narrowed per the owner's quoted decision; the narrowing is recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-17-non-goal-veterinarian-directory-filtering.md and in the Non-Goals table. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn; the Superseded entry and the stale known-defect edge case in the Veterinarian directory section were updated to point at REQ-VET-003. Three open questions recorded rather than waited on: whitespace trimming of a non-blank filter, a repeated filter parameter, and a future visible control. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR — that file is outside my write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter extends the existing vet feature package: no new package, no new type, no new route. VetRepository gains a whole-name case-insensitive lookup by specialty in paged and unpaged form, mirroring OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith; VetController takes the filter as a request parameter and selects between the filtered and unfiltered read. Three things are new ground and are now recorded. First, the filtered reads must NOT carry @Cacheable("vets"): the vets cache is created with no expiry and no size limit, so a caller-supplied key would grow it without bound (ADR 2026-09-17-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-vets-cache). Second, the paging links must carry the filter through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, never the __${...}__ preprocessing idiom the file uses today for page numbers; preprocessing splices the value into the expression before parsing, which turns a request parameter into template-expression source (ADR 2026-09-17-request-values-in-links-use-link-expression-parameters, system-design § View Templates). Third, system-design had no § Scale and Load section at all; it now exists with rows for both directory forms and for owner search. Contracts rows for Vets, VetRepository, and VetController now cite REQ-VET-003, and the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less is removed — that surface is now supported. Claims rest on direct reads of VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, CacheConfiguration.java, vetList.html, and OwnerController.java; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so reads are the basis rather than symbol resolution.
integration_points: Entry point /vets.html: the specialty filter binds as a String request parameter, request-scoped, with no persisted type bound. No form object and no new binder — VetController binds page as a plain parameter today and the filter joins it the same way.
Entry point /vets: same String request parameter on the existing @ResponseBody route; the response stays the Vets wrapper, unpaged.

Boundary, repository, in the controller tests: the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository in VetControllerTests continues as the double. It is a framework stub, justified because the controller tests verify routing, model population, and the filtered/unfiltered selection — not query semantics. Stub the new filtered methods there alongside the two existing findAll stubs.

Boundary, repository, in a new repository test: no double. Matching semantics (whole name, case-insensitive) live in the derived query and a stub cannot demonstrate them, so a new @DataJpaTest-style VetRepositoryTests runs the real query against the real H2 seed data (radiology, surgery, dentistry). This test, not the controller test, is what proves theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreLetterCase and theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchPartOfASpecialtyName.
Boundary, framework transport: MockMvc, the project's one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy), unchanged from the existing vet tests.
Cache boundary: the two existing findAll methods keep @Cacheable("vets"); the new filtered methods carry no cache annotation. CacheConfiguration is not touched.

patterns.description: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) — the parameterized paged derived query this slice mirrors. Use equality with IgnoreCase over the specialties association rather than StartingWith, since the PRD requires whole-name matching.

The empty-search normalization: an absent or empty value means the broadest read. Note one deliberate difference — OwnerController strips the value, and this slice must NOT strip. The PRD requires that spaces around an otherwise valid specialty name are preserved and therefore match nothing, while a blank value behaves as absent. The test is isBlank() for the absent case, with no strip applied to a non-blank value.

Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted shape is binding, not a business rule. The blank-means-unfiltered branch is therefore admissible in the controller and does not extend the recorded controller-holds-rules deviation. The matching semantics stay in the query, not the controller.

The paging block to change. Every link there uses __${...}__ preprocessing today; the specialty must travel as a link-expression parameter instead. The page-number links may keep preprocessing or move to the parameter form, but the specialty never uses preprocessing.

risks.risk: Unbounded growth of the vets cache if the filtered reads are annotated @Cacheable("vets"). The cache has no eviction and no size limit (CacheConfiguration builds a bare MutableConfiguration), and the route is unauthenticated like every route here, so the key space would be caller-controlled. Cited row: system-design § Scale and Load, 'Veterinarian directory page, filtered by specialty'; system-design § Threat Model, 'Unbounded cache growth from caller-supplied keys'.
risks.mitigation: Leave the new repository methods uncached, per ADR 2026-09-17-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-vets-cache. Simplest readable form: a plain derived query. The path is bounded by clinic staff size, so the uncached read costs one indexed query.

risks.risk: Expression injection if the specialty reaches a paging link through __${...}__ preprocessing, which parses the spliced text as an expression. Output escaping does not reach this: the injection is into the template engine, not the rendered page. Cited principle: docs/security-principles.md § Realization, cross-site-scripting row (default escaping stays on) — this decision extends that row to expression construction, which the brief does not currently name. Recorded in system-design § View Templates and § Threat Model.
risks.mitigation: Build the filtered links as @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. The engine URL-encodes the value and never parses it, which also makes a specialty containing a space or ampersand round-trip correctly.

risks.risk: Matching semantics drift between the two forms. /vets.html and /vets must resolve the same filter identically, and a stubbed repository in the controller test cannot catch a divergence in the query itself. Cited principle: docs/testing-principles.md test pyramid and CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy, minimal mocking.
risks.mitigation: Both controller methods call the same pair of repository methods, and the repository test exercises the real query against the H2 seed data. Do not implement the filter by post-filtering a findAll() result in the controller — that would place a matching rule in the controller and break paging arithmetic.

risks.risk: Paging arithmetic over a filtered set. totalPages and totalItems must come from the filtered Page, not from the unfiltered count. Cited row: system-design § Scale and Load, filtered directory row.
risks.mitigation: Route both branches through the existing addPaginationModel so the model is populated from whichever Page was read; add the specialty to the model so the template can carry it into the links.

risks.risk: The eager @ManyToMany on Vet.specialties combined with a join-filtered paged query can duplicate rows or shift the page window if the join is expressed as a fetch join. Cited row: system-design § Scale and Load, filtered directory row; system-design § Persistence, eager fetch under disabled open-in-view.
risks.mitigation: Use a derived query traversing specialties.name so the filter is a WHERE join and the eager association is loaded by its own select. Assert the expected page contents in the repository test rather than only the element count.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so nothing to audit. Doc writes this dispatch: system-design gained § Scale and Load and § View Templates, two Threat Model rows, three Contracts rows citing REQ-VET-003, a qualified provenance banner, and the removal of the machine-readable-route Known Defect (the PRD already struck it). Two ADRs written. docs/adr/README.md gained index rows for both, plus the missing row for the product expert's non-goal ADR that the prd-entry flagged — that file is in this agent's write scope, so the gap is closed. The non-goal ADR itself (docs/adr/2026-09-17-non-goal-veterinarian-directory-filtering.md) was written by product-requirements-expert and is not claimed here. Brief gap to surface, not silently fixed: docs/security-principles.md § Realization has no row for template expression construction — its XSS row governs rendered output only. That brief is outside this agent's write scope; the rule is recorded in system-design § View Templates with an ADR back-link, and the security brief should gain a matching row when its owner next edits it. The three open questions the prd-entry recorded stay open and are not decided here: whitespace trimming of a non-blank filter is settled by the PRD acceptance criterion (no trimming), a repeated specialty parameter is undefined behavior and no test should pin it, and a visible control is a later request.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the new filter reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java:72 `Collection<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String name) throws DataAccessException;` and :82 the Pageable overload). `grep -rn -F -e "nativeQuery" -e "createQuery" -e "@Query" src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/` returns no match, so no query text is built from the request value.

Cross-site scripting and template-expression evaluation: the request-derived `specialty` is never spliced into a Thymeleaf preprocessing expression. vetList.html:34 reads `th:href="${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=${i})} : @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}"` -- a link-expression parameter, URL-encoded by the link expression and attribute-escaped by `th:href`, against a fixed literal path (no `javascript:`/`data:` reachable). The change also removes the pre-existing `@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}` preprocessing from all five pagination links, a strengthened control, not a weakened one. `grep -rn -F -e '__$' src/main/resources/templates/` leaves hits only in fragments/inputField.html, fragments/selectField.html, fragments/layout.html and owners/ownerDetails.html, all on application-controlled values (field names, menu links, `owner.id`), none touched by this change.

Cache key space / unbounded allocation: both new repository methods are deliberately not `@Cacheable("vets")` (VetRepository.java:62 comment; `grep -n "Cacheable" VetRepository.java` shows the annotation only on lines 45 and 55, the two unfiltered reads). Caller-supplied text therefore cannot mint entries in a cache that has no eviction policy. docs/system-design.md:203 records the matching threat-model row.

Mass assignment: the slice adds no request-bound object. Both handlers take `@RequestParam(required = false) String specialty` (VetController.java:46 and :77), a scalar, so no binder allow-list question arises.
Credentials: `git diff` across the change set, filtered for added lines matching password/secret/token/api key/credential, returns no match. No new credential enters the repository.

Supply chain: build.gradle and the Gradle wrapper are unchanged in this change set, so the slice adds no dependency. OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured (`grep -in "dependencycheck" build.gradle` finds nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review; the declared framework version is Spring Boot 4.1.1 (build.gradle:5 `id 'org.springframework.boot' version '4.1.1'`).

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The same two-branch conditional — `${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=X)} : @{/vets.html(page=X,specialty=${specialty})}` — is copy-pasted across all five paging links (sequence links, first, previous, next, last), differing only in the page value X. This is the exact pattern `code-quality-review` § Control Flow flags: "A conditional repeated across sibling sites (code, template elements, links) is duplication: compute it once (th:with or a fragment) and reference it." A future change to how the filter is carried (e.g. adding a second query parameter) has to be applied identically in five places, and a reader has to verify by eye that all five copies actually agree.
findings.fix: Extract a Thymeleaf fragment parameterized by the page number, e.g. th:fragment="pagingLink(page)" that builds the href from `page` and the page-scoped `specialty` model attribute, then th:replace/th:insert it from each of the five call sites instead of repeating the ternary.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: vetList.html:26-47 converts five independent paging-link render sites (the page-number loop, first, previous, next, last) from __${...}__ preprocessing to @{...} link-expression parameters, a change the ADR (docs/adr/2026-09-17-request-values-in-links-use-link-expression-parameters.md) treats as an expression-injection mitigation, not cosmetic. The test exercises only currentPage=1/totalPages=2 (via aPageHolding(helen(), TWO_MATCHING_VETS) with ONE_VET_PER_PAGE=1), under which the first- and previous-page links never render (th:if="${currentPage > 1}" is false) and are therefore never exercised at all. The single assertion is content().string(containsString(SECOND_PAGE_LINK + "&specialty=radiology")) — an OR across whatever renders (here the loop link, the next link, and the last link all happen to produce the identical page=2 href), so a regression in any one of those three sites (e.g. one link left on the old preprocessing idiom) would not fail the test as long as at least one of the others still renders the correct string. theUnfilteredVetListPagingLinksShouldCarryNoSpecialty has the same currentPage=1 gap for first/previous, though its not(containsString("specialty=")) assertion is an AND over the whole page and is not weakened by the aliasing.
findings.fix: Request a middle page (e.g. page=2 of 3, or a Page built with totalVets sized to put currentPage strictly between 1 and totalPages) so first, previous, next, last, and the two loop links all render simultaneously with distinct expected hrefs, and assert each individually (or assert the full rendered href for each anchor) rather than one shared substring.

approved_aspects: VetRepositoryTests.java is a real @DataJpaTest against the H2 seed data (data.sql: vet_id 3=Douglas and 4=Ortega both hold specialty_id 2='surgery'), correctly placing the matching-semantics rule (whole-name, case-insensitive, no substring match, no space-trimming) at the repository seam per the design-block's assignment rather than behind the controller's mocked repository — theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreLetterCase, theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchPartOfASpecialtyName, and theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotIgnoreSurroundingSpaces exercise the real derived query

author: change-grader
summary: filter both vet list surfaces by specialty

blast_radius.note: One module (src) and the vet feature package: two Java files, two templates, two test files, plus docs. No sensitive paths, no config, no schema, no cross-cutting change; the 47 hunks are mostly docs and tests (293 test lines against 102 prod lines).

semantic_surprise.note: Two residuals a filter-sized description would not predict. The change rewrites all five paging links of the pre-existing unfiltered directory from the __${...}__ preprocessing idiom into a new shared fragment wrapped in th:block, so the unfiltered page's link construction changed too (asserted identical in tests, but it is a rewrite, not an addition); and the new paged derived query joins the to-many specialties association with no distinct, so Page.getTotalElements and page membership rely on specialties.name being unique, which the schema does not enforce (src/main/resources/db/h2/schema.sql:19-21 declares name VARCHAR(80) with a plain index). Unreachable with the seeded data and with no write path for specialties, but uncovered by any test.

test_adequacy.note: Tests are real, not tautological: a new @DataJpaTest VetRepositoryTests runs the actual derived query against the seeded H2 data for whole-name, case-insensitive, partial-name, padded-name and empty-result cases plus paged counting, and VetControllerTests asserts each of the five rendered paging anchors individually on a middle page for both the filtered and unfiltered lists, including a negative assertion that the unfiltered page carries no specialty= at all.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved in round 2 with no findings and no recommendations, and spot-checked citations resolve exactly (docs/system-design.md:134 and :63, docs/ubiquitous-language.md:52, docs/security-principles.md:20, docs/prd.md:123, vetList.html:33/40/46/52/58). One does not: the doc-reviewer cites docs/adr/README.md:144-146 for the three new index rows in a 75-line file where they sit at 73-75. The claim itself is true on inspection, so this reads as a clerical locator slip rather than a fabricated fact, but it is an approval carrying one citation that does not resolve.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake-decision line by line: NG-9 narrowed with its own non-goal ADR, /vets reinstated under a fresh REQ-VET-003 with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn and its id unreused, filter as a URL contract with no page control added, paging links carrying it. Zero build retries, zero consultations; the second design-block is a doc-only fix pass, not a re-triage.

rationale: Read the template hunks and the new repository query before merging. The paging links of the unfiltered directory were rewritten into a fragment, not merely extended, and the paged specialty query joins a to-many with no distinct over a name column the schema does not constrain. Both are benign on seeded data and untested beyond it.
